items.title: Does Ka'wa'ill need his own token to pass the Aegis of the Hearth?
items.context: The Aegis is specifically designed to exclude magical creatures — and Ka'wa'ill, the merfolk companion, is one. Wilhelm (a non-covenant human) gets a token via Éogan's Arcane Connection; it's unclear whether the same trick works for, or is even offered to, Ka'wa'ill.
items.raised_event: Casting the annual Aegis of the Hearth near Harfleur
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25) from ArM5e core (armdef-0.4-spells-vim, Aegis of the Hearth; armdef-0.4-long-term-events, Warping). Yes — more fundamentally than Wilhelm. Ka'wa'ill is a Might creature, and RAW "No foreign supernatural creature with Might, of any type, can cross the boundary of the Aegis unless its Might exceeds the level of the Aegis." To enter he must either be made a native ("Anyone who participated in the ritual to cast the Aegis is a native of that Aegis") or be explicitly excluded ("The ritual also allows certain individuals to be excluded from the effects of the Aegis"); the covenant's token is the tracking device for that. A plain human like Wilhelm needs a token only so his own supernatural powers are not suppressed inside; Ka'wa'ill needs exclusion to cross at all. CONDITIONAL on q025: the Aegis is currently recorded at level 0 — if that is genuinely 0, any Might>0 creature already "exceeds the level" and crosses freely, making the token moot. Settle q025 to finalize.

items.title: Who is “V.,” and did they ever reach the covenant?
items.context: An unsigned letter to Solving Epicurusson, found in the GM's prep notes but never surfaced at the table or reflected in the chronicle. Addressed by courier (Mercere or trusted equivalent), it references a prior vis dispute off Saint-Valery touching the holdings of “a Tytalan recluse,” and a contact in Leuven who once gave Solving access to the Duke's private seals and warned him when Rhine Quaesitors began asking questions. The writer says their title has since been revoked and their name is now a cautionary tale in Tribunal chambers — the Rhine has become untenable, and they ask whether Solving's offer of “a covenant in motion, unanchored and burdened less by the weight of Tribunal demands” still stands. They sign only “—V.” and say they'll wait within sight of Saint Jacob's bell tower in Bruges, near the fish-market stairs, for three more cycles of the moon. Given Solving's own disappearance in Bruges in 1220, the timing may or may not be a coincidence — unclear whether this was ever meant to be picked up, or whether V. and Solving's vanishing are connected at all.
items.resolution: Already answered in verified_events.json's "Sorting through Solving's letters and documents / Finding 'V'" event: the same letter is quoted verbatim, Dagmar had Garrat Coffin investigate, a magically-tainted brooch tied to a recently-worn magus turned up, and city-guard records confirmed "the Duke's men removed someone without city sanction." The event states outright: "Rumors indicate that a man matching the description was abducted by men in the livery of the Duke of Brabant." V. never reached the covenant — likely abducted.

items.raised_in: GM's Notion prep notes (undated), "The Situation with Valerian"
items.resolution: Canon set by GM (2026-07-25), reconciled with play-record in verified_events.json + magi.json. THE CONSPIRACY: a sect of magi from the RHINE TRIBUNAL has suborned the BISHOPRIC OF LIÈGE from within (verified_events event 60, "Valerian's Revelations") — a massive breach of the Code of Hermes (magi controlling Church hierarchy), using the Church as their proxy. It is NOT the loose "Duke of Brabant + Church" shorthand some notes use. VALERIAN: Valerian de Castellane, a Guernicus/Quaesitor of the Rhine Tribunal (magi.json), was investigating this when he was silenced and imprisoned by the Duke of Brabant — the capture happening IN BRUGES, which is politically sensitive and could provoke a response if known. The Church, acting for the Rhine magi, requested the capture; the Duke complied out of obligation to the Church and the Holy Roman Empire. Valerian had been compiling a case to bring to the GRAND TRIBUNAL. He escaped via a delayed teleportation spell hidden in the 'V' letter (nested Rego/Creo Vim), materializing on the Scholar's Wake 55 days later (events 51, 60). He is technically still a Quaesitor but "not allowed to practice"; his library is largely contraband confiscated from magi studying forbidden topics; he holds knowledge that could "ruin a lot of people's day," and traded protection to Valdemar for access to it. STILL LIVE (deliberately open): Valerian's current motivations and next move — now on the run — are unclear, to be driven by play. Whether the Liège conspiracy is ever exposed/contained is likewise open. DOWNSTREAM: this reframes c023 (the Duke's motive was obligation/coercion by Church+HRE, not merely believing forged authority) and gives t028 (Reynald, still GM-prep-only, 0 play hits) its likely role as the Rhine-trained hand inside Brabant's court. t011 (Dagmar seeing Valerian's contraband trade) is the same contraband library.

items.title: Why was Ka'wa'ill exiled from merfolk society?

items.resolution: Canon set by GM (2026-07-25): Ka'wa'ill's exile is really a SELF-exile driven by pride. Staying in merfolk society meant accepting a standing in the court hierarchy lower than his pride could accept, so he left rather than swallow the demotion. Fits his status as a Knight (the lowest order of the Noble caste) and his "merman prince" self-regard, and reconciles with the Exiled Atlantean flaw, which applies whether the departure was involuntary or chosen — here it was chosen.

items.title: Look up how spontaneous magic integrates with the Boundary target.
items.context: GM note (2026-07-14) — flagged for rules research.
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25) from ArM5e core: the Boundary target forces a spell to be a Ritual (the enchantment rules note "no other reason for the spell to be a ritual, such as Year duration, Boundary target, or major effect"), and Ritual magic cannot be cast spontaneously. Therefore spontaneous magic cannot use the Boundary target at all.

items.title: Tormente's errand: carry the golden crown to the estranged dragon-kin off NE England to earn passage into the Carnac regio.
items.context:
Raised session 2026-07-25 (proposed_events p052). The Carnac sea-cave regio's first threshold is guarded by TORMENTE, a magnitude-10 dragon (magic resistance in the 50s) blocking the only way deeper. Rather than fight, Dagmar parleyed a PRICE: Tormente handed him a heavy jewelled golden crown (Roman in style) to carry as an OFFERING OF PEACE to its estranged kin — another dragon that 'will not speak to me,' dwelling in a sea-cliff cave ABOVE the waves off the English northeast coast, near Scarborough / Newcastle, just short of Scotland. Reconcile the two, and Tormente will deem Dagmar worthy of passing deeper into the regio. Dagmar accepted and gave orders to sail NORTH — probably via Stonehenge to collect Llewellyn and finally cash in the time-crystal en route (see t018). OPEN QUESTIONS TO DEVELOP: (a) the kin's disposition — why the estrangement, and whether a crown actually mends it or the kin is hostile; (b) 'Jeffrey the First' — Tormente asked whether Dagmar served this long-dead king of Brittany, whose 'quest of learning' it seems to guard; who he was and why the regio's guardian tests seekers in his name is unexplained; (c) the wrinkle that Foxglove robbed Tormente's hoard the same night (c026), which could sour the goodwill this errand depends on. This is Dagmar's active quest; t025 (the regio proper) stays gated behind it.

DEVELOPED (session prep 2026-08-08, q027 #4): the 'estranged kin' is MÍMORMR, a cursed bone-speaking scholar-wyrm off the NE English coast (full detail in the new t072). The errand is not what it looks like: Tormente is a TRICKSTER, the Roman crown is the KEY that BREAKS a curse Tormente itself laid, and carrying it 'in peace' actually UNBINDS Mímormr — who becomes a regional environmental threat once loose. Dagmar is an unwitting cat's-paw; completing the errand earns passage into the regio (t025) at the region's expense. Mímormr's false-but-sincere claim to descend from Jörmungandr, and the NE-England wyrm-legend tie, are in t072.

items.title: What are we preparing for next session?
items.context:
As of the end of Spring 1224 the party is split across two threads — Wilhelm & Éogan making their way home from Ireland, and Dagmar running north from the half-opened Carnac regio (proposed_events p047–p054). This is the GM's working slate of candidate scenes to develop and stage for the next session. The answers so far:

1) WHAT DO WILHELM'S ASSISTANTS BRING BACK — AND COULD IT NEGATE THE HYPOTHESIS? Wilhelm's research assistants were sent west and south over the winter (p049), paid in grain and silver, to gather hedge-tradition material. The beat is what they return with at the rendezvous — and specifically whether any of it FALSIFIES the folk-magic thesis rather than confirming it: a tradition that works WITHOUT leaning on the environment (the inverse of the Uisneach augury insight, p047), or the open-ocean storm-prediction / current-finding citation the thesis still lacks (t009) turning out not to exist, or to cut against the 'context and time-of-year matter' core (t019). A negative result forces Wilhelm to revise before he can deliver to Scarem Montem (see #6). Cross-ref t009, t019. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the negation is a MADNESS failure rate that breaks the scalable/vis-factory case without disproving the magic (t019, t020, q028); the assistants also flag a temporal hedge mage who beat the Limit of Time, leaving Wilhelm an origin-less brass acorn (t071).]

2) WHERE DOES FOXGLOVE GET OFF THE SHIP? Foxglove is aboard carrying roughly five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold (c026), lifted the same night Dagmar agreed to run Tormente's peace-errand (t066). She has every reason to disembark and vanish with the hoard before the theft surfaces — and the Tide of Memory is already running north up the English coast toward a Stonehenge-Tribunal port (p054), an obvious jumping-off point. Settle at which port she gets off (and whether she deserts outright), and what the fallout is if she is still aboard when Dagmar returns to Tormente and the missing hoard is noticed. Cross-ref c026, t066. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: these are player calls; what got prepped is the WORLD constraint — a GM reference on converting Roman gold c.1224 (no gold coinage / silver standard, so bullion-by-weight only; melt, goldsmiths, Jewish moneylenders, Flanders/Lombard bankers, worked goods, the Church; treasure-trove and provenance friction; no collector market yet) now lives in c026.]

3) DOES VALDEMAR JOIN DAGMAR FOR THE DRAGON LEG? The northbound errand — carry the jewelled crown to Tormente's estranged kin off Scarborough / Newcastle (t066) — is a two-magus job waiting to happen. Dagmar has already invited Llewellyn ex Miscellanea by Redcap (p054); Valdemar Bjornsson, a PC magus with no familiar yet (t037) and an established tie to the sea-fae Rán (c022), is a natural companion for dragon diplomacy. Decide whether Valdemar signs on, what he brings, and how his Rán connection reads to a dragon claiming Norse descent (see #4). Cross-ref t066, t037, c022. [DEFERRED 2026-08-08: Valdemar's player has been absent; GM to improvise whether he joins rather than prep it in advance.]

4) THE KIN-DRAGON CLAIMS TO BE A CHILD OF JÖRMUNGANDR. The reveal waiting behind t066(b): the estranged dragon off the English northeast coast (or Tormente itself) claims descent from Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent — styling itself the greatest magical being that ever was. For a Norse-seiðr saga this is a major cosmological escalation — it recontextualizes the Carnac regio's guardianship, the unexplained 'Jeffrey the First / quest of learning' hook, and frames Tormente's magnitude-10 Might as merely the lesser sibling's. Decide how literally true the claim is, what Might / scale it implies, and how it lands against the saga's existing Norse threads (Rán, the sea-fae). Cross-ref t066. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the claim is FALSE but sincerely believed by MÍMORMR, a cursed bone-speaking scholar-wyrm; Tormente (a trickster) is using Dagmar to break its curse, and freeing it looses a regional threat — full build in the new t072.]

5) ÉOGAN AND THE CAPRICORN. Already logged as GM intent (t070): on the sea voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' thread (t068) escalated to a Might-bearing creature and offered as his first familiar prospect (t037). The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond. Placement: the Spring/Summer 1224 voyage home. Cross-ref t070, t068, t037. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: draw is independent of the t068 fae affinity; signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES; mythological grounding (Enki's Goat-Fish / Macrobius's Gate of the Gods), corpus build/bind references, and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build all recorded in t070. What it wants in exchange remains open.]

6) DOES WILHELM SAIL TO SCAREM MONTEM? The ship-for-book swap is confirmed in motion — the Hound of Cassel is under Wilhelm's control and headed back to Scarem Montem (t002, Resolved) — and what he owes them is the folk-magic thesis. The delivery scene therefore hinges on #1: whether the assistants' material firms up (or breaks) the thesis's weakest citation (t009) decides whether Wilhelm arrives with a finished thesis or one still short a maritime example. Cross-ref t002, t009. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the three sealed chests aboard the Hound of Cassel (c012) are now defined — intercepted Bishopric-of-Liège↔Scarem Montem cipher letters exposing a Church/State suborning (Code violation, tied to the Brabant conspiracy t028/c023/t027). Ring-based public/private-key crypto means the covenant can PROVE the correspondents but mostly can't read the content. Wilhelm may be carrying Scarem Montem's own incriminating mail back to them — return, keep, or weaponise it in the swap?]

Update (2026-08-10) — refocused for the 22nd (into Fall 1224). With #2/#3/#4 and the Rody hand-off now PLAYED (see the Chronicle), the next-session slate narrows to three spines: (A) Wilhelm's delivery run to Scarem Montem — the thesis gate #1 (s1) feeding the delivery #6 (s6); (B) Dagmar's push into the regiones gated behind Tormente — the return with Mímormr's token (s8), Llewellyn's time-flow gambit (s9), and the wider regio cluster (s10); and (C) a NEW home-front spine — Confluensis turning the screws (s11, t078), the soured-liege reprisal (c019/c022) finally going active while the magi are scattered. items.title: Foxglove robbed Tormente's dragon-hoard without sanction — while Dagmar is courting the same dragon's favor.
items.context:
Raised session 2026-07-25 (proposed_events p053). The night after the parley, the grog FOXGLOVE (scout/rogue, avaricious) quietly took the rowboat back into the Carnac cave alone, dived the cave floor, and smuggled roughly FIVE BAGS of spilled gold aboard — mostly Roman-style coin, priceless — hiding it for herself and lying past Peter (a clean Guile 'caught red-handed' success) about running an errand for Dagmar. Angus meanwhile spun a broadly-honest dragon tale to the 16 crew for drinks. THE PROBLEM: this is an unsanctioned theft from a magnitude-10 dragon's hoard, committed the very night Dagmar agreed to run Tormente's peace-errand (t066) and is depending on the dragon's goodwill to pass deeper into the regio (t025). Neither Dagmar nor Tormente knows yet. Consequence seed: if Tormente notices missing hoard on Dagmar's return, the errand's welcome could curdle. Kept Open.

GM REFERENCE (prep 2026-08-08, developing q027 #2) — CONVERTING ROMAN GOLD c.1224. Governing fact: England and NW Europe are on a SILVER standard in 1224 — the silver penny is the coin, and there is NO circulating gold coinage (Henry III's gold penny doesn't come until 1257, and fails). So the Roman coin has no face value anywhere Foxglove can go; it is worth only its WEIGHT in gold as bullion (gold:silver roughly 1:10–1:12), which still makes five bags set-for-life money IF she can convert it without being robbed, taxed, or hanged. Realistic channels: (1) MELT to anonymous bullion at a goldsmith's crucible — destroys the coins' identity, the safest move for a thief, at the cost of the smith's cut; (2) sell/pledge raw gold to a town GOLDSMITH or moneyer (London, York, Newcastle) for silver; (3) JEWISH MONEYLENDERS (London, Lincoln, Norwich, Canterbury — this is pre-1290 expulsion), the era's professional bullion/pledge dealers and the natural discreet fence; (4) ITALIAN / LOMBARD / CAHORSIN bankers, best reached at the FLANDERS FAIRS / BRUGES on the covenant's own trade routes; (5) commission it into WORKED GOODS (rings, brooch, plate) — portable, disguised, origin hidden; (6) the CHURCH / a MONASTERY buying gold for reliquaries, plate, gilding, illumination (also a laundering route via commission or donation). Complications: TREASURE-TROVE law — found hidden gold of unknown owner belongs to the CROWN, so she cannot declare it (honest story = confiscation, dishonest = theft charge), which is exactly why melting appeals; the PROVENANCE problem — a grog flashing Roman aurei in a Stonehenge-Tribunal port is a walking question mark, reputable buyers ask, discreet ones charge for not asking; and weight/portability aboard a 16-crew ship. NOT options: there is NO antiquarian coin-COLLECTOR market yet (numismatic collecting is a Renaissance development, Petrarch a century later); and the coins cannot be spent AS coin north of the Alps. Irony to hold: the best discreet bullion channels (Flanders bankers, the trade net) are the COVENANT'S own — which she cannot use, because she is hiding this from the covenant; laundering pulls her toward the very people who'd recognize the gold. (Where she gets off, whether she's caught, and what she does with it remain the player's calls.)

Update (2026-08-08 session): Advanced. In London, Foxglove could not spend gold in a silver economy; a fence converted only a little (three coins) at a punishing one-for-one (a silver pound per gold piece). She keeps the bulk. She is ALSO wanted elsewhere, so she means to stay close to the covenant for cover while holding the hoard — setting up a reckoning when Dagmar returns to Tormente.

items.title: Valdemar's title to the Isle of Man — the owed favour, the fief, and the Christian lie.
items.context:
GM note 2026-08-15. Valdemar has quietly secured right and title to the Ránargarðr holding on the Isle of Man through a private arrangement the covenant knows nothing about: a big favour done for Rǫgnvaldr Guðrøðarson (Reginald), the Norse-Gaelic Christian King of Mann and the Isles, a down payment made in goods or services, and title received in writing. He wants to hold the land in fact, not merely by sword-right, and to keep the local potentate a friend — though that ruler's ENEMIES are fair game — chief among them Rǫgnvaldr's own rival brother, Óláfr “the Black,” who has forced a partition of the Kingdom of Mann and, with Norwegian and Church backing, is angling to oust him. The open question is the FORM of the obligation — an Oath of Fealty (which Valdemar would rather avoid) versus a promise of specific service — and the standing DEBT it leaves him owing, which the GM may call in at any time.

Next-session beat (scene s14): the fief is granted — potentially as a proper feudal fief — but Valdemar must LIE and profess himself a Christian to receive and hold it. That deception stacks on his hidden House Diedne lineage (t078): a pagan viktir magus, secretly Diedne, now also perjuring his faith to a Christian-facing authority to hold mundane land openly. Rich exposure if it ever unravels.

Longer arc (player-flagged, optional): Valdemar may later move to own the Isle outright — unseating Rǫgnvaldr with the complicity of the King of Norway — the same Norwegian backing that, historically, lifts his brother Óláfr over him — if the other magi take interest.

Settlement plan: recruit grog families first, then island/mainland settlers wanting new farmland to clear, then other pirates and their families; a Norse 'bailiff' to run the place while Valdemar raids and trades; justice dispensed by Valdemar as local lord when in port; and a winter Althing for community decisions — a Viking fjord-town in the making around Nóatún. The player's full hand-off is in the dossier below.

Rules aside (the player's question — 'no rules about Hermetics ruling land openly in our Tribunal, right?'): there is no blanket Hermetic ban on owning or ruling mundane land, but the Oath's clause against interfering with mundanes and thereby bringing ruin on one's sodales is the lever a quaesitor would reach for — openly ruling a fief is deep mundane entanglement. Whether it crosses the line is a Tribunal call, and this border sea-covenant already runs on unusual mundane latitude (see the Normandy 'Mundane Goods Are Fair Game' custom). Plausible — but it widens his exposure. Cross-ref t079 (the manor & lab), s13/s14, and t078 (Confluensis and the Diedne secret).

Update (2026-08-21) — the Ránargarðr site carries a confirmed Magic aura of 3 (see t079), low enough that the growing fjord-town can be settled without Warping its people. Note also that the Diedne Garden is NOT part of this holding: it lies on the Channel's south coast (t082).

Update (2026-08-23, verified play): the survey and the approach to the local Norse lord for legitimate title are now the verified (Incomplete) 'Establishing a dock and base on the Isle of Man' event — Valdemar chose and named Ránargarðr at Laxey and sought the lord, but the grant/fief and its terms remain unresolved. sections.heading: The Storyteller's decisions & rulings
sections.body:
Ruled 2026-08-15, after walking the build against the Covenants lab rules.

— VIKTIR & THE LABORATORY —

Viktir rune-workings function as SPELLS: in place of Technique + Form they use the relevant rune Abilities in the Lab Total. So learning/inventing a rune-spell-effect is the "Spells" lab activity — enhanced by the Antechamber's +3 Spells and by General Quality.

Imbuing an object with a rune is a DISTINCT activity, handled exactly as enchanting an object with a spell: the "Items" activity — enhanced by the +3 Items (Forge + Running Water + Superior Tools) and by General Quality. Both of Valdemar's chosen Activity specializations (Spells AND Items) are therefore load-bearing for his own practice, which is why picking both is coherent rather than scattered.

General Quality (+1) adds to every Lab Total except Teaching and Texts (Covenants p.110). Art specializations add only to workings that use that Art — so Rego/Aquam help his Diedne Hermetic magic, not his rune-work (unless a slot is pointed at a rune; see below).

Effective lab bonuses:
 • learn/invent a rune-spell-effect ....... +4 (Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • imbue an object with a rune ............ +4 (Items +3, GQ +1)
 • invent a Diedne Rego Hermetic spell .... +5 (Rego +1, Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • invent a Diedne Aquam Hermetic spell ... +5 (Aquam +1, Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • enchant a device (Hermetic) ............ +4 (Items +3, GQ +1)

— SPECIALIZATIONS: PLAYER'S CHOICE OFFERED —

Because runes are a viktir magus's functional "Arts," the lab's four Art-specialization slots may be pointed at RUNES instead of Hermetic Techniques/Forms. The player may choose, per slot, rune-based or Technique/Form-based specialization:
 • A terrain/purpose feature grants the rune associated with it — e.g. the seaside Idyllic Surroundings can grant Laguz (the water-rune) in place of Aquam.
 • A free-choice feature (Dedicated Building) may pick either a rune or a Hermetic Art (currently Rego).
He stays under the 2-Activities + 4-Arts cap either way (he uses only 2 Art slots).

— THE BUILD, RATIFIED —

Size 13 — 9 points spent on features, 2 Empty holding 4 points in reserve for future Refinement. Legal; the cost is paid in Safety and silver.
Safety 0 (features +9 − occupied size 9). Superior Construction doubles the outlay: 100£ to build (100 lab points × ½£, doubled).
General Quality +1; Aesthetics +11 (≈55-point Rune-Master reputation); Health 0; Warping 0.
Refinement 0 for now (capped at Magic Theory 3; rises with study).

— UPKEEP: CORRECTED TO 4 —

Dedicated Building's +1 Upkeep counts, so Upkeep = 4 (not 3) = 100 upkeep points. Per the Points of Laboratories table (Covenants), yearly maintenance = points × season-use multiplier ÷ 10:
 • ≤1 season/yr: ×0.5 → 5£/yr
 • 2 seasons/yr: ×1.0 → 10£/yr
 • 3-4 seasons/yr: ×1.5 → 15£/yr
Valdemar works the lab mostly in Winter (one season), so baseline upkeep is 5£/yr.

— CONSTRUCTION: CORRECTED TO 100£ (2026-08-15) —

The build cost tracks the same lab-points total that drives upkeep. Correcting Upkeep 3 → 4 raised that total 60 → 100 points, so construction rises with it: 100 points × ½£, doubled by Superior Construction = 100£. (The player's original notes above read 60£ — the earlier 60-point / Upkeep-3 figure.) Confirmed against the Covenants conversion (titterpig-dsl-arm5e): the Points of Laboratories table sets Upkeep +3 = 60 and +4 = 100; the build cost is one pound per two points, doubled by Superior Construction. Covenants' own worked example — raising Upkeep +2→+4 (a +70-point jump) costs 35£ — matches exactly.

— THE NAMES (CANON) —

Ránargarðr ("Rán's Garden") — the seaside harbour holding acquired for the manor; likely the name of the village that grows around it.
Nóatún ("Place of Ships," Njord's seaside hall) — the covenant's main Hall on the Isle of Man, where the coven Winters.
Undrahöll ("Hall of Wonders") — the hall housing Valdemar's laboratory and his and Rán's living quarters, living space kept separate from the lab for Safety.

— PENDING —

Final specialization picks (rune vs Technique/Form, per slot) are the player's to make.
Construction (60£) and upkeep are funded through the raiding/trading seasons and booked in the covenant ledger; hold the actual build seasons until the specs are locked.

items.title: How does the covenant price enchanted items bought from Verditius crafters (e.g. Wilhelm's stone sled)?
items.context: Wilhelm wants to buy a stone sled (a single L20 flight/haulage effect, a ~2-tonne slab) at Durenmar for Terram vis (p104). RAW: a Verditius crafter's sale price is “twice the vis necessary to make it, in addition to the vis required for the project” (HoH:MC) — the worked wand example shows this is 3× the vis ACTUALLY spent making the item (opening + instilling). The Verditius Craft reduction (ArM5 Core p.93) reduces only the OPENING cost, “to a minimum of one pawn.” Two build paths give very different answers, and the Craft-discount question only arises on one of them.
items.resolution:
Ruling (owner, 2026-09-20). Two parts:

1) BUILD MATTERS. A single-effect item like the sled is naturally a LESSER enchanted device: its cost is the instilling cost alone — one pawn per ten levels — with NO opening step (Core: “there is no need to spend any Vim vis to prepare the item”). So a L20 sled costs 2 pawns to make, and — because the Craft reduction only touches OPENING — there is nothing for a Craft discount to reduce. Sale price = 3 × 2 = **6 pawns of Terram vis**, flat, discount or no. This is the sled's price (p104).

2) HOUSE RULE (greater/invested devices only). If an item is instead built as a GREATER/invested device it must be opened to its full vis capacity first (Material × Size, p.97; an item cannot be “partially” opened), and there the Verditius Craft reduction can slash a large opening cost to a minimum of one pawn. For those builds the covenant computes the 2× markup on the UNDISCOUNTED opening cost — the crafter keeps the Craft efficiency as profit rather than passing it to the buyer. (Doesn't affect the sled, which is a lesser device.)

items.title: What Level/Quality are the standard “Roots” (foundational Art summae) the covenant can acquire?
items.context: Covenants (p.93, Standard Texts) describes the Roots but gives no numbers; a Redcap can arrange delivery “for a very small consideration.” By their description they must be at least L5/Q15. Wilhelm hopes to source one or more at Durenmar (p104).
items.resolution: Ruling (owner, 2026-09-20): the covenant's standard Roots are adopted as **L6 / Q24** summae, Redcap-deliverable for a small consideration. Q24 leaves cushion for quick apprentice copies (Juvenalia, ~-3 quality, stay readable). Exceptional Roots (L7/Q28, dragonskin-bound) are treated as effectively unobtainable in play. A specific Root enters the library only when actually acquired.

items.title: Blessing of the Fine Harvest — confirm mechanics (Wilhelm)
items.context: Acreage re-checked against the definitive DSL: the Creo Herbam Level-1 guideline ('ensure a plant grows well') already bakes in a +3 Size enhancement (affects a plant up to ten paces / a large tree ≈ 1,000 pace³). With the sheet's added +3 Size (×1,000) and a further +1 magnitude, that is +7 Size magnitudes total = ×10^7 ≈ ~2,000 acres of standing crops — so the '2,000 acres' figure is broadly correct (SG size estimates are intentionally rough). REMAINING MECHANICS TO CONFIRM: (1) the '+1 part (sizable to target)' should be a +1 SIZE magnitude, not Target: Part — Part affects part of a single whole, it is not a size multiplier; (2) a field of many separate crop-plants is really Target: Group (or Boundary, which requires a ritual), not Individual — a Group of the same mass costs +1 magnitude over the Individual calc, so a RAW-clean field version is +5 levels higher; (3) Moon duration keeps it formulaic and the effect reverts after a month (a growth boost, not a permanent harvest); (4) adding AL+PH to a FORMULAIC spell needs the Ceremonial Casting Spell Mastery (no initiation) or the folk mechanic — fine in Wilhelm's context.
items.resolution: Ruling (owner, 2026-09-30): finalized as CrHe base 1 (the Level-1 guideline already includes +3 Size) + R: Touch (+1) + D: Moon (+3) + T: Individual + **+3 Size** = Level 20. The +3 Size on the guideline's built-in +3 is six size magnitudes in all (×10^6 by mass), giving a scope of ~200 acres. The spell affects a SINGLE crop type at a time; to cover MULTIPLE crop types, switch to Target: Group for +1 magnitude (Level 25). Moon duration keeps it formulaic; AL+PH is added via Wilhelm's folk-caster system (or the Ceremonial Casting Spell Mastery for a standard magus). Mass-scaling basis: arm5e spell-rules 'Targets and Sizes' (×10/magnitude by mass) + the CrHe Level-1 guideline's built-in +3 Size; the acres figure is a troupe estimate under the book's explicit 'a rough guess is fine' allowance.

Legal status is a deliberately fuzzy area; the covenant decided to hold them "for now," prepared to return them if Scarem Montem comes asking. Never revisited since. (Worth noting: Normandy Tribunal custom holds it's legal to raid non-magical items from another covenant — part of why keeping the chests was even a live option rather than an obvious violation.)

Update (2026-07-25) — GM: still unexplored; contents NOT yet defined. To be figured out once the open-questions backlog pass is complete (flagged for end-of-pass follow-up, alongside t032). Includes deciding the wrinkle: do the chests return with the Hound of Cassel (now going back to Scarem Montem under Wilhelm, t002), get kept/opened first, or become their own negotiation. Kept Open.

CONTENTS DEFINED (2026-08-08, developing q027 #6). The three chests hold MISSIVES from the BISHOPRIC OF LIÈGE to SCAREM MONTEM — correspondence in which Scarem Montem is exploring a similar SUBORNING OF CHURCH OR STATE, a wild violation of the Code of Hermes (interfering with the mundanes / meddling with the Church). Liège being a prince-bishopric adjacent to Brabant, this ties directly into the existing conspiracy web: the Duke-of-Brabant / Church infiltration (t028 Reynald de Grimbergen, c023, t027) and the Lotharingian-Tribunal manoeuvring (t010, t017). The letters were intercepted IN TRANSIT (Summer 1221 piracy) and never reached their recipient.

THE CIPHER — magical public/private-key cryptography via MATCHED RINGS. Each correspondent holds a pair. Enclosed WITH each letter is a ring that functions as the SENDER'S PUBLIC KEY: the recipient wears it to VERIFY WHO WROTE the letter (an unforgeable signature). The recipient's OWN ring is their PRIVATE KEY: it DECRYPTS letters that were written to them — but only letters the sender composed while holding that recipient's public-key ring, so that only the matching private ring can read them. Reading a letter thus needs BOTH: the enclosed sender-ring (to verify) and the intended recipient's private ring (to decrypt).

WHAT THE COVENANT ACTUALLY HAS: the letters plus the enclosed LIÈGE (sender) public-key rings — but NOT Scarem Montem's PRIVATE rings, which stayed with the intended recipient. Consequence: they can VERIFY authorship and so hold UNASSAILABLE PROOF OF AT LEAST ONE PARTY — that the Bishopric of Liège was corresponding with Scarem Montem, and which Liège hands signed — even though they generally CANNOT read the ciphertext itself. Getting plaintext would require capturing Scarem Montem's private ring, coercing a decrypt, or a hard magical break (Intellego Vim / Mentem against a cipher likely built so only the intended mind can read). The rings are themselves magical items now in the covenant's possession.

THE SCENE-6 WRINKLE: these chests are Scarem Montem's own property, riding Scarem Montem's own stolen hull (the Hound of Cassel), which WILHELM is now sailing back to Scarem Montem to settle the ship-for-book/thesis debt (t002). So Wilhelm may be about to hand Scarem Montem back the very (mostly-unreadable) evidence that proves them guilty of a hanging-level Code violation — unless he realises what he carries and keeps it as leverage in the swap, or turns it over to the Tribunal / the Brabant-conspiracy investigators. Open: does Wilhelm know what's in the hold, and does he return, keep, or weaponise it? Kept Open.

MOTIVE LINK (2026-08-08): this is a hidden cause of Scarem Montem's rushed TRIBUNAL ESCALATION. Their incriminating Liège correspondence went missing with the pirated ship (the Hound of Cassel) and they never learned what became of it — so, unable to risk their Church/State-suborning plans being exposed and not knowing who held the evidence, they FORCED THE PACE at the 1223 Normandy Tribunal (see verified event 'Scarem Montem steals the Tapestry and declares for Lotharingia', 1223-06-26, and Bridget's Lotharingian pitch, t010): moving openly for Lotharingia and seizing the Tapestry rather than playing the long game. In hindsight their haste reads as a tell — they were running scared of exactly what is sitting in these three chests. The covenant still doesn't know it holds the leash.

Update (2026-08-08 session): Found and secured. Wilhelm discovered the three sealed boxes aboard the Hound of Cassel (his new ship) at the Isle of Man. They remain magically sealed and UNOPENED in-fiction (the Liège-cipher content above is GM prep, not yet revealed). Legal status: taken in Valdemar's raid on a Scarem Montem vessel; magical goods are protected by the Code, so they were held in trust and never returned — now awkward since Scarem Montem left the Tribunal. Wilhelm laid a month-long Vim ward on the hull as a deterrent/legal fig-leaf.

Update (2026-08-23, verified play): RETURNED. On the Summer 1224 delivery run (verified 'Wilhelm returns the Hound of Cassel and recovers his thesis'), Wilhelm handed the three still-sealed chests back to Scarem Montem — sealed and UNREAD, apparently without the covenant ever realizing what they held; the Liège-cipher contents above were GM prep and never surfaced in-fiction. GM OPEN NOTE (Scarem Montem): the covenant has unknowingly handed its own leverage straight back — Scarem Montem holds the incriminating Liège correspondence again and the covenant kept no copy. The Church/State-suborning plot and the Liège tie can still be resurfaced later (if the covenant learns what it briefly held, or the correspondence surfaces elsewhere). Kept Open as a latent thread.

items.title: Scarem Montem kept Wilhelm's thesis for a year and is deploying it against Montverte's villeins.
items.context:
PROVENANCE (already in canon). At the 1223 Tribunal, Hilda gave FETTELMID of Scarem Montem the LATIN copy of Wilhelm's folk-magic thesis for a 'cursory appraisal by end of day Friday.' Hilda's own plan went no further than swinging by the tent to assess whether extended review was warranted. Scarem Montem left Montverte with the manuscript in their baggage and nobody chased it. t020 already describes the situation as Wilhelm retrieving his 'stolen thesis' — this entry records what they did with it.

THE YEAR. By Wilhelm's Summer 1224 delivery run (s6) they have held the text roughly twelve months: replication over Fall 1223, first field deployment by Winter/Spring 1224, casualties on the ground before he sails. A year is more than enough to have independently found the madness rate that Carl and Isaac found (see q028) — and they continued. That is the moral distinction between them and Wilhelm.

THE TARGET. They are deploying it against VILLEINS IN TERRITORIES CONTROLLED BY MONTVERTE — their own liege. Bridget of Scarem Montem pitched Éogan on the Lotharingian Tribunal at the 1223 Tribunal; destabilising Montverte's mundane base weakens the liege ahead of the Grand Tribunal petition. Run it as a GIFT rather than an experiment: the technique offered to selected villeins as folk wisdom, in villages they want turned. The madness is the point and it is deniable, because it presents as the countryside going strange on Montverte's watch.

WHY THEY STILL WANT A HANDOVER. A formal delivery LAUNDERS THE POSSESSION — it makes Wilhelm author of record and the transmission consensual and witnessed. A later quaesitorial inquiry then finds a Hermetic magus who gave it freely in payment of a debt. The swap is a signature, not a purchase.

WILHELM'S COUNTER-WEAPON. Teaching the ungifted is his exposure; it is also theirs, at scale, with intent, against mundanes. He holds a real charge.

THE LOOSE VERIFIER. JULIANA ex Bonisagus at Dragon's Rest holds the Low German copy and expects to swap for the Latin post-Tribunal. She does not know it has been in the field for a year. A Bonisagus, at a covenant Montverte is trying to poach, who can detonate this with no PC involvement.

SUGGESTED REVEAL VECTOR (not at Scarem Montem): Wilhelm's assistants, already out west and south gathering citations, return having found the technique ALREADY IN USE in a village that should not have it, with the same failure rate. He recognises his own method in the field before he reaches the door.

items.title: Mímormr, the cursed bone-speaking wyrm — Tormente's errand is a jailbreak.
items.context:
Developed from q027 #4 (session prep 2026-08-08), resolving the 'estranged kin-dragon' hook inside t066. MÍMORMR (Mím-, echoing Mímir the severed head of wisdom who speaks knowledge of old things, + ormr, 'serpent') is the kin-dragon dwelling in a sea-cliff cave above the waves off the English NORTHEAST coast (Scarborough / Newcastle, just short of Scotland). It is a SCHOLAR-WYRM: a researcher of ancient things that SPEAKS WITH BONES (interrogates the dead / ancient remains), curious and deeply frustrated, and — critically — it can no longer LEAVE ITS HOLE, because TORMENTE cursed it to stay put many, many years ago.

THE CLAIM: Mímormr styles itself a CHILD OF JÖRMUNGANDR, the greatest magical being that ever was. This is FALSE — but it is true that Jörmungandr existed (Rán may even know a rumor of it; see c022), and Mímormr SINCERELY BELIEVES the descent. Its conviction is motivated reasoning that is genuinely EARNED: questioning ancient bones, it found real traces of Jörmungandr and over-read authentic scholarship into a personal genealogy. A true researcher who reached a false conclusion because it wanted to. The magi therefore cannot easily disprove it — the evidence is real; only the inference is wrong.

THE TRAP: Tormente is a TRICKSTER (mischievous, and can be cruel). The 'reconciliation' errand (t066) is a lie — the Roman crown is the KEY that BREAKS THE CURSE, and Tormente is using Dagmar, a passing Criamon, as an unwitting cat's-paw to loose the thing it caged, keeping its own claws clean. Delivering the crown in good faith earns Dagmar passage deeper into the Carnac regio (t025) at the price of UNBINDING Mímormr — and the party won't know until it's done (open: can they discover the truth in time?).

THE CONSEQUENCE: freed, Mímormr becomes an ENVIRONMENTAL THREAT to the region — not necessarily hostile to the magi, but catastrophic to be near. GM flavor to pick/stack when activated: a sea-wyrm whose passage floods coasts and sinks hulls; a bone-speaker whose curiosity cracks open barrows and rouses the restless dead; storm-weather in its wake (fits the Carnac regio reading 'more Auram than Aquam'); or an aura/vis-draining apex predator that blights the stretch of coast it settles on. REAL-WORLD ANCHOR: the English northeast is worm-legend country (the Lambton Worm, the Sockburn Worm, the Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh) — a loose Mímormr can SEED or BECOME the origin of those Northumbrian dragon-legends.

TO DEVELOP when activated: Mímormr's Might / statblock (Tormente is magnitude-10 and was strong enough to cage it — set Mímormr's relative power; a Magic-realm dragon); the exact release mechanics of the crown; whether and how the party can learn the truth before acting; and whether Foxglove's unsanctioned hoard theft (c026) tangles in. Cross-ref t066, t025, c022, c026, t018.

STATBLOCK BASIS (2026-08-08): build Mímormr on POLYMATHES, THE DRACONIC LIBRARIAN (Realms of Power: Magic p.76; present in the merged corpus) — a dragon whose avarice is for KNOWLEDGE, not gold, hoarding rare and ancient lore. Base chassis to keep: Might 41 (Animal), Size +7, Int +5 / Pre +8 / Str +12 / Sta +8; Essential Flaw Avaricious (major) + Inquisitive; the scholar kit (Educated, Arcane Lore, Second Sight, Gift of Speech, Magic Lore 6 'ancient magic', Philosophiae 6, Artes Liberales, Latin/Greek/Arabic); the InMe 'Peering Into the Mortal Mind' power (reads the mind of anyone it can see); Poisonous Blood (CrAq); and the telling 9 Intellego vis in the heart. Note Might 41 sits BELOW Tormente (build Tormente on STELLATUS, the Dragon — Might 50, MR 50 = magnitude-10), which is why Tormente could cage it. ADAPTATIONS to make it Mímormr: (1) hoard = ancient BONES and relics, not books; (2) replace Polymathes's Master of Illusion focus with a 'SPEAKS WITH BONES' Intellego focus (Corpus/Mentem, interrogating the dead) — the Intellego heart-vis fits a diviner exactly; (3) the false Jörmungandr-descent belief falls straight out of Magic Lore 6 + bone-divination (real traces of Jörmungandr, over-read into a personal genealogy — genuine scholarship, wrong inference, so the magi can't easily disprove it); (4) reskin the squat golden mountain-lizard into a long serpentine SEA-WYRM in the Scarborough/Newcastle sea-cliff cave, keeping Poisonous Blood (Aquam) and optionally reskinning Fiery Breath to a storm/brine breath to match the Carnac regio's Auram lean; (5) the curse ('cannot leave its hole') is an EXTERNAL binding Tormente laid, broken by the Roman crown — not an innate stat. Freed, its Size +7 bulk and restless curiosity are the regional threat (sunk hulls, flooded coasts, barrows cracked for bones, storm-wake).

STATTED (2026-08-08): full playable sheets for TORMENTE (on the Stellatus chassis, Might 50) and MÍMORMR (silver/aquamarine sea-wyrm, Might 41, briny-north-wind breath) are now in npcs.json as 'entity' statblocks.

Update (2026-08-08 session): The reveal played out. Mímormr is a giant silver-and-aquamarine worm who sincerely claims descent from Jörmungandr and 'speaks with the bones of the dead'; Tormente disputes the ancestry and called its deeds wicked. Delivering Tormente's crown broke the binding and FREED it — it means to finish work here, then head east into the North Sea to seek a relative's bones. Now a loose threat (see c027). The binding proved non-Hermetic (see q029).

Update (2026-08-23, verified play): played — Mímormr freed. The crown proved a name-release undoing Tormente's binding; Mímormr took it and emerged. It reached for Dagmar's mind (in truth to crush his skull) but Dagmar slipped it with his Parma while Mímormr believed it succeeded. Loosed, it means to finish here and make east to the North Sea ancestor. See c027.

items.title: Which Roots did Wilhelm bring back from Durenmar? Enter them in the library at L6/Q24.
items.context:
Wilhelm's declared 1225 Durenmar trip (p104) includes sourcing one or more Roots — the standard foundational Art summae, adopted as L6/Q24 and Redcap-deliverable “for a very small consideration” (ruling q034). The specific Arts are the owner's call and have not been chosen.

**FOLLOW-UP:** once the trip is played, decide which Root(s) Wilhelm obtains, add each to the covenant library at L6/Q24 (covenant_ledger.json library.books), and log the “small consideration” cost.

**Update (2026-10-03 session):** played. Wilhelm ordered the Roots at Durenmar and brought them home without difficulty. The GM has the list in a separate file. **FOLLOW-UP:** add each title to the library at L6/Q24 and log the 'small consideration' cost. The nine-Arts problem in the Durenmar scene (only nine Arts have a Root; the fifteen titles there are placeholders) still applies.

**OWNER RULING (2026-10-04):** the nine Arts with Roots are Auram, Intellego, Herbam, Rego, Animal, Ignem, Aquam, Vim and Muto. Of these, **Intellego, Muto, Herbam, Ignem and Animal** were available at Durenmar. Spare copies lying around are unlikely; copying them, paid for in vis, is probably easy. Still to settle: how many Wilhelm took, and how.

**WHAT THE SOURCES SAY:**

- *Covenants* (Standard Texts): the Roots 'are widely and cheaply available. A Redcap can arrange the delivery of any of these texts, for a very small consideration.'
- *Covenants* (Prices for Books, Sound Books): copies 'charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book’s level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced. A surcharge of up to 20% is added if there is a spare copy available for the impatient.' For a Level 6 summa that is 6 pawns and a season's wait. The Roots are explicitly cheaper than ordinary books, so their price should sit below this.
- *Covenants* (Mundane Books): 'Any magus with a spare pound can have any standard text from a stationer in a large city.' This sits under mundane books, so it may mean mundane standard texts rather than the Roots.
- *Guardians of the Forests* (the Great Library): 'Visitors to the Great Library are not permitted to take its books outside its walls, nor to copy them, without the explicit permission of the librarian.' But 'House Bonisagus and members of the covenant are also exempt from all these requirements' (the contribution rules). Copies 'can be scribed in the library, for which materials are provided.' The librarian sees 'little need for low-level or mediocre-Quality summae… since the library already has a glut of such texts.' A copy can be requested by Redcap 'accompanied by a payment of vis to cover the cost of scribing. However, the covenant is notoriously slow at fulfilling such requests.'
- *Core* (copying): 'Every season that a character spends copying a summa carefully, she accumulates points equal to 6 + her Profession: Scribe score. When she has accumulated points equal to the level of the summa, it has been copied.' Quickly: 'she gains 18 + 3 times her Profession: Scribe score points towards copying a summa. Books copied quickly have a quality one lower than the book copied.'

**WHAT THAT MEANS HERE:** Hilda, Wilhelm's scribe, has Profession: Scribe 4 in Foundry (80 xp). Copying quickly she makes 18 + 12 = **30 points a season: all five Level 6 Roots in one season, each at Quality 23.** Copying carefully she makes 10 points a season, enough for one Root at full Quality 24. One season with a Root takes any Art below 6 up to 6.

**OPTIONS:**

- **(a) Hilda copies them at Durenmar.** Wilhelm (Bonisagus, with a lab there) gets the librarian's permission and Hilda copies all five quickly in Spring 1225 while he builds the sleds, using the library's materials. Cost: her season. **Recommended.** It matches the table ('no problem getting a copy of the Roots') and costs no vis.
- **(b) Durenmar's scribes copy them for vis.** At the Sound Books rate it would be 6 pawns each (30 for five) and a season's wait, but the Roots' 'very small consideration' argues for less — say 1 pawn each. Your price.
- **(c) Redcap delivery later**, for 'a very small consideration' — the route for the four Roots Durenmar didn't have (Auram, Rego, Aquam, Vim).

**FOLLOW-UP:** pick the route and the price, then add the copies to the library at L6/Q24 (or Q23 if copied quickly).
items.resolution: Resolved 2026-10-04 (owner): option (a). With the librarian's permission, Hilda copied the five Durenmar Roots (Intellego, Muto, Herbam, Ignem, Animal) quickly in Spring 1225 — 30 points, one season, no vis — and they are in the covenant library at Level 6 / Quality 23. The other four Roots (Auram, Rego, Aquam, Vim) remain available by Redcap for 'a very small consideration', price unset. Hilda's season is not yet in the XP tracker (1225 seasons aren't reviewed).

items.title: Furtum: is there a vis-to-silver exchange rate, and is Technique vis worth more?
items.resolution: Resolved (owner's answer to Furtum's player, 2026-10-06): (1) Vis is almost never traded for silver. If you can find a buyer, the price varies, sometimes considerably. About 10 Mythic Pounds a pawn will do if you are trying to count your wealth, but, like stock in a private company, theoretical value and what you get in a sale are very different. (2) Vis is generally traded for goods in kind, or for favors or seasons of work. Technique vs Form (owner, 2026-10-06): 5 Form = 3 Technique, from the Normandy Tourney rate in The Lion and the Lily, adopted as a GM decision. Recorded on the Reference page (Homebrew: 'Vis and Silver — What a Pawn Is Worth').
items.context:
Furtum's player asks (2026-10-06): do we have a vis-to-silver exchange rate, and is Technique vis worth more than Form vis? Owner's inclination: vis is not exchangeable for money directly.

**WHAT THE BOOKS SAY**
- *Covenants*, 'The Price of Vis': 'It is almost impossible to put a fixed monetary price on a pawn of vis. Magi prize vis, their currency of choice, far more highly than silver. Most consider that mundane things should be bought with silver, and magical things with vis, and that is indeed usually what happens.' Also: 'For this reason, the trading of vis for silver is rarely undertaken, although it is not unheard of, especially amongst House Mercere'. Prices run 'between a couple of pounds to a hundred or more pounds per pawn, depending on such factors as geographical location, the particular Art of the vis, the wealth and whims of local covenants and magi'. But 'a base guideline of roughly ten pounds per pawn is a reasonable rule of thumb for a typical saga.'
- *Houses of Hermes: True Lineages* (Mercere): 'most of Europe does not recognize vis as having a monetary value like silver or gold.' And: 'If circumstances warranted, ten pounds of silver might be considered roughly equivalent to a pawn of vis, as an Orderwide starting point for negotiations'.
- **Technique vs Form, Normandy precedent.** *The Lion and the Lily*, Tourney prizes: 'One prize pawn may be traded for an immediate once-only selection of 5 pawns of Form vis, or three pawns of Technique vis.' In this Tribunal, Technique vis counts for about 5:3 against Form.
- On record: the covenant has traded vis for vis (the Redcaps trade, Winter 1224-25) and paid vis for magic (Wilhelm's stone sleds).

**RECOMMENDATION:** keep the owner's inclination as the rule. There is no market and no standing rate, and vis does not convert to silver at will. A sale is a story: find a buyer (a Redcap broker, a wealthy covenant, a Verditius), at about 10 pounds a pawn as the opening figure, moved by place, Art and need. Technique vis is dearer by Normandy custom (5 Form = 3 Technique). This also keeps the covenant's Poverty hook meaningful.
